issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\pi \not\in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}}$ (or non-singular covariance of $\nu$) to the statements of parts (2) and (3) of Theorem 2.3.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that violating $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{dec}}$ alone prevents eigenvalues with $|\lambda| < 1$, and that violating $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ alone prevents non-identity unit-circle eigenvalues, is false without assuming $\pi \not\in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}}$. Corollary 2.4 remains sound because it assumes all three conditions together.
issues.title: Omission of non-singular covariance hypothesis in Theorem 2.3 parts (2) and (3)
issues.why_classification: Restricting parts (2) and (3) of Theorem 2.3 by requiring $\pi \not\in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cov}}$ restores validity without altering the global proof architecture, but narrows the advertised standalone scope of the individual symmetry conditions shown in Figure 2.1.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.4 claims $\mathrm{F} = \mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}} \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$. The proof deduces that the stable subspace $V_s$ must be trivial, arguing that otherwise $p^\top \overline Z = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \lambda^k (q^\top Y^{(k)} + w^\top d(Y^{(k)})) + b$, which it claims contradicts $\pi \in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}^{\mathrm{c}}$. However, when $p \in V_s$ is orthogonal to the support of $Z$, $p^\top \overline Z = 0$ a.s., and with $q=0, w=0$, the relation reduces to $0=0$, which yields no contradiction and does not place $\pi$ in $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$. Consequently, $A$ can have eigenvalue 0 and be singular. Any distribution where $d(Y)$ is nonlinear but lies in the null space of $A$ while $Z$ is supported on the range of $A$ satisfies $L_{\pi, y_\star}(X, Y) = AX + d(y_\star) = Z + d(y_\star)$, giving exact weakly $y_\star$-dependent affine conditioning. For instance, in $n=2, m=1$ with $Y \sim \mathrm{Uniform}([-1, 1])$, $Z = (Z_1, 0)^\top$ with $Z_1 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, and $d(y) = (0, y^2)^\top$, the update with $A = \mathrm{diag}(1, 0), B = 0, c(y_\star) = (0, y_\star^2)^\top$ is exact, so $\pi \in \mathrm{F}$, yet $\pi \not\in \mathrm{E}^{\mathrm{EnKU}}$ (as $d$ is nonlinear) and $\pi \not\in \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$ (since $Z_1$ has unbounded support while $Y$ is bounded).

failure_location.quote:
The set of all $\pi \in \Pp_2\left(\R^n\times \R^m\right)$ that have a weakly $y_\star$-dependent exact affine update decomposes as 
$$
\mathrm{F} = \mathrm{E}^\mathrm{EnKU} \cup \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}.
$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restrict $\mathrm{F}$ to conditioning maps where $A$ is non-singular and impose non-degeneracy conditions on the joint measure, or substantially expand $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$ to include all degenerate-rank transports, which would defeat the claim that $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$ is a small symmetry class.
issues.overall_effect: The main optimality theorem of Section 3 and the abstract's core claim—that the EnKU achieves near-maximal exactness among all weakly $y_\star$-dependent affine conditioning maps up to the narrow class $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$—is false. The set $\mathrm{F}$ contains a broad class of nonlinear models admitting exact rank-deficient affine conditioning.
issues.title: False characterization of the maximal exact set F in Theorem 3.4
issues.why_classification: Theorem 3.4 is one of the paper's principal theoretical results. Its characterization fails on a large class of nonlinear models, and fixing it requires either major loss of advertised scope or significant architectural revisions to the definition of $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{nl-dec}}$.
